key_insight: ActionRAG improves LLM long-term memory by refining retrieved evidence through query-conditioned graph diffusion rather than relying solely on initial similarity scores.
engineering_relevance: The architecture targets agents that must recover precise, mutually consistent facts and relationships from growing interaction histories.
method: Reconcile type labels and apply tiered entity resolution during indexing.
Retrieve entities and triples through dual channels to construct a bounded local evidence graph.
Refine triple scores with receiver-normalized diffusion, seed protection, hub penalties, and triple materialization.
evidence_signal: On MemoryAgentBench’s eight deterministic-scoring columns, ActionRAG averages 55.1 accuracy, beating the strongest retrieval-based memory baseline by 5.4 points; mean synthesis cost is below $0.001 per query on four reported cost columns.
watch_item: The reported 440.7 ms sums separately measured retrieval-side p99 components on consumer Apple Silicon; it is not an end-to-end p99 latency measurement.
paper_title: ActionRAG: Evidence-Refining Graph Diffusion for Long-Term Memory in LLM Agents
